subject: maths
title: Perfect squares and difference of two squares

scenes.heading: Perfect squares and difference of two squares
scenes.sub: Two shortcuts that save you time
scenes.say: Some brackets come up again and again. In this video you will learn two patterns that let you expand them in seconds: perfect squares and the difference of two squares.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A square lawn with a path along two sides
scenes.breaks: Lengths are never negative, but in algebra b can be, which makes the middle term negative.
scenes.say: Picture a square lawn of side a, with a path of width b along two sides. The total area is the lawn, a corner tile, and two strips of path. That is why a plus b, all squared, has two a b pieces in the middle.

scenes.heading: Why there are two middle pieces
scenes.say: First the square is drawn, then its sides, a plus b. Inside are four pieces: a squared, two pieces of a b, and b squared. So a plus b, all squared, equals a squared plus two a b plus b squared.
scenes.caption: First the square, then its sides, a + b. Inside are four pieces: a², two pieces of ab, and b². So (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

scenes.heading: Perfect squares
steps: Double the product of the terms
scenes.say: For a perfect square, remember: square, double, square. Square the first term, double the product of the two terms, and square the last term. The last term is always positive.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Expand (3x − 2)².
scenes.say: Expand three x minus two, all squared. Square the first: nine x squared. Double the product: negative twelve x. Square the last: positive four. So the answer is nine x squared minus twelve x plus four.
scenes.caption: Expand (3x − 2)². Square the first: 9x². Double the product: −12x. Square the last: +4. So 9x² − 12x + 4.

scenes.heading: Difference of two squares
notes: Big square a², cut out b²
scenes.say: Now a square of side a is drawn, and a small square of side b is cut from the corner. The shape left has area a squared minus b squared. Rearranged, it is a rectangle a plus b by a minus b. So the middle terms cancel, and you just get a squared minus b squared.
scenes.caption: A square of side a, with a square of side b cut out. The shape left has area a² − b². Rearranged, it is a rectangle (a + b) by (a − b), so (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

scenes.heading: Mental maths trick
scenes.question: Work out 41 × 39.
scenes.say: Here is a neat trick. Forty-one times thirty-nine is forty plus one, times forty minus one. That is forty squared minus one squared: sixteen hundred minus one, which is fifteen ninety-nine.
scenes.caption: 41 × 39 is (40 + 1)(40 − 1). That is 40² − 1²: 1600 − 1 = 1599.

scenes.say: Quick recap. For perfect squares: square, double, square. For a plus b times a minus b, the middle cancels and you get a squared minus b squared. And always square the whole term. Now try the practice questions!
